from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: The Prisoner's Dilemma", [
            "A warden challenges two prisoners with 64 coins.", 
            "One coin hides a key under the board.", 
            "They must identify the coin to survive."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        alice = Circle(radius=0.3, color=WHITE).set_fill(WHITE, opacity=0.5)
        bob = Circle(radius=0.3, color=WHITE).set_fill(WHITE, opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(alice, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(bob, "D2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(alice), FadeIn(bob))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        box = Rectangle(width=2.5, height=1.5, color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(box, "C5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(box))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        confess = Text("Confess", font_size=20, color="#00FFFF")
        silent = Text("Silent", font_size=20, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(confess, "C4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(silent, "C6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(confess), Write(silent))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "We assign a unique binary index to each square.",
            "Alice treats the board as a 64-bit string.",
            "She calculates the parity of all heads-up coins.",
            "Flipping one coin changes the total parity.",
            "This forces the board to reveal the secret."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Mapping the Board to the Information Space", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        board = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.5, color=GREY_B) for _ in range(16)]).arrange_in_grid(4, 4, buff=0.1)
        # Using a 4x4 representation for visualization clarity within 6x6 grid
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(board))
        self.place_in_area(board, "A1", "D4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        bits = VGroup(*[Text(str(i % 2), font_size=15) for i in range(16)])
        for i, bit in enumerate(bits):
            bit.move_to(board[i].get_center())
        self.play(FadeIn(bits))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        key_sq = board[7]
        key_sq.set_fill(color="#FF00FF", opacity=0.5)
        self.play(Indicate(key_sq))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(board[10].animate.set_fill(color=YELLOW, opacity=0.8))
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Alice uses the board as a communication channel.",
            "Changing parity points exactly to the hidden key.",
            "Bob reads the board to recover the coordinate.",
            "They survive with absolute, mathematical certainty.",
            "The strategy transforms a guess into pure logic."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Solution: Communication through State Change", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create a simple chessboard representation
        board = VGroup()
        for i in range(4):
            for j in range(4):
                square = Square(side_length=0.7, fill_opacity=0.5, color=BLUE)
                square.move_to(np.array([i*0.7 - 1, j*0.7 - 1, 0]))
                board.add(square)
        
        self.place_in_area(board, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(board))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Indicate parity flipping (visualize as color change in one square)
        self.play(board[5].animate.set_color(RED))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Visualizing signal
        signal = Circle(radius=0.3, color=YELLOW).move_to(board[5].get_center())
        self.play(Create(signal))
        self.play(FadeOut(signal))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GREEN)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Logic transforms uncertainty into a solved puzzle.",
            "This principle powers modern error correction protocols.",
            "Information theory bridges abstract math and reality."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: The Power of Information Theory", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        bit_group = VGroup(*[Text(str(i % 2), font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF") for i in range(10)])
        bit_group.arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(bit_group, "B2", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(bit_group), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        logic_text = Text("Error Correction / ZKP", font_size=24, color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(logic_text, "D4", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(logic_text), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        final_msg = Text("Information Theory = Reality", font_size=28, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(final_msg, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(final_msg), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(*self.mobjects))

outline.topic: The Impossible Chessboard: Information Theory in Action
outline.target_audience: University students (CS/Math majors or curious minds)

sections.title: The Hook: The Prisoner's Dilemma
sections.content: Introduce the problem: A warden forces two prisoners to play a game. A chessboard with 64 squares is filled with 64 coins (Heads/Tails). The warden hides a key under one square. One prisoner identifies the square; the other must guess which one it is to survive. How can they ensure survival with 100% certainty?
sections.example: Visualize two characters, 'Alice' and 'Bob', standing on opposite sides of a giant 8x8 grid of glowing coins.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Parity Bit (Information Foundation)
sections.content: Explain the concept of 'Parity'. Parity is the simplest form of error-detecting code. If we have a set of bits, the parity bit tells us if the count of '1's (Heads) is even or odd. This is the fundamental unit of information compression.
sections.example: Show a row of 3 coins: [H, T, T]. If H=1 and T=0, the sum is 1 (odd). Adding a parity bit of 1 makes the total sum even. Graphical animation: A 'checksum' balance scale.

sections.title: Mapping the Board to the Information Space
sections.content: Apply the math: Assign a binary number (0-63) to each square. Treat the state of the 64 coins as a 64-bit string. Alice can calculate the parity of the current board state. By flipping exactly one coin, she can force the parity of any subset of squares to match the target secret square.
sections.example: Visual overlay: An 8x8 grid where each square has a coordinate index. Alice performs a XOR summation of the binary indices of all 'Heads' coins.

sections.title: The Solution: Communication through State Change
sections.content: Alice communicates one bit of information by changing the parity of the entire board to point to the secret square index. Bob, seeing the new board configuration, calculates the parity and recovers the exact coordinate of the key.
sections.example: A 2D animation showing the 'parity vector' pointing to the hidden key square as Alice flips one coin.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Power of Information Theory
sections.content: Reflect on how this bridges logic and information. We didn't 'guess'; we used the board as an information channel. This illustrates the principle of 'Zero-Knowledge Proofs' and Error Correction, which are vital for modern computer networks.
sections.example: Final shot: Alice and Bob walking free, with the chessboard dissolving into binary code (1s and 0s) floating in the air.
